records.title: Symplectic integration: a canonical map, not an exact energy promise
records.section: Symplectic integration: a canonical map, not an exact energy promise
records.text: A symplectic integrator advances a Hamiltonian system while preserving its canonical two-form. This is the map property behind the good long-time behavior of many orbital and particle integrators. It does not generally preserve the original Hamiltonian exactly. The Hamiltonian map notebook separates those two questions with computed examples.

records.title: Symplectic integration: a canonical map, not an exact energy promise
records.section: What the map preserves#
records.text:
For state z = (q,p), Hamilton’s equations and the symplectic condition are
\dot z=J\nabla H(z),\qquad J=\begin{pmatrix}0&I\\-I&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad D\Phi_h(z)^T J D\Phi_h(z)=J.
The last identity says that each numerical step is a canonical transformation. For one degree of freedom it is equivalent to det(D Phi) = 1, preserving oriented phase-plane area. In higher dimensions, preservation of total volume alone is weaker than symplecticity.
Three separate properties should be tested: preservation of the two-form, preservation of H, and time symmetry Phi_(−h) = Phi_h^(−1). Symplectic Euler already illustrates the distinction: it is symplectic but is neither exactly energy preserving nor time symmetric in general.

records.title: Symplectic integration: a canonical map, not an exact energy promise
records.section: Split the Hamiltonian, compose exact subflows#
records.text:
For a unit-mass separable system H(q,p) = p²/2 + V(q), the two subflows are a drift and a kick:
D_h(q,p)=(q+hp,p),\qquad K_h(q,p)=(q,p-h\nabla V(q)).
Each is symplectic; compositions remain symplectic. The notebook includes kick–drift symplectic Euler, and the symmetric second-order Störmer–Verlet update
p_{n+1/2}=p_n-\frac h2\nabla V(q_n),\quad
q_{n+1}=q_n+h p_{n+1/2},\quad
p_{n+1}=p_{n+1/2}-\frac h2\nabla V(q_{n+1}).
This is the mechanical Leapfrog/velocity-Verlet formulation. It differs from the two-step scalar recurrence in the earlier time-integration notebook.

records.title: Symplectic integration: a canonical map, not an exact energy promise
records.section: Fourth order by composition#
records.text:
Writing S2(h) for a Verlet step, one fourth-order composition is
S_4(h)=S_2(a h)\,S_2(b h)\,S_2(a h),\qquad
a=\frac1{2-2^{1/3}},\quad b=-\frac{2^{1/3}}{2-2^{1/3}}.
Yoshida (1990) develops higher-order symplectic compositions. Here b is negative: an internal substep goes backward in time. The construction is suitable for the smooth conservative examples used here; simply applying it to irreversible diffusion, shocks, or collision handling is not justified. Higher order also does not establish unconditional stability or an equal-cost advantage.

records.title: Symplectic integration: a canonical map, not an exact energy promise
records.section: Energy and a modified Hamiltonian#
records.text:
Backward error analysis describes a nearby, generally formal modified Hamiltonian. Under smoothness, bounded-trajectory, small-step, and related hypotheses, this explains small long-time energy errors. It does not assert an exact invariant of the original H for every orbit or step size. Hairer, Lubich, and Wanner (2003) develop this geometric viewpoint and its assumptions.
For the special oscillator H = (p²+q²)/2, kick–drift–kick Verlet preserves the quadratic invariant
I_h=\frac12p^2+\frac12\left(1-\frac{h^2}{4}\right)q^2
up to roundoff. H itself oscillates. This invariant is not a claim that its unscaled Hamiltonian flow is exactly the numerical time-h map. The oscillator map is bounded for |h| < 2; above that limit it can be symplectic and unstable.

records.title: Symplectic integration: a canonical map, not an exact energy promise
records.section: Implicit midpoint and RK4 as comparisons#
records.text:
Implicit midpoint is symplectic and time symmetric when its endpoint equation is solved accurately. It preserves the quadratic oscillator H to roundoff here. It need not exactly conserve a nonquadratic H. Classical RK4 is fourth order but is generally neither symplectic nor time symmetric. Good short-time accuracy alone does not certify the map’s geometry.
The second test problem is H = p²/2 + q²/2 + q⁴/4, a smooth nonlinear oscillator. It makes midpoint’s special quadratic-energy conservation visibly distinguishable from a general claim.

records.title: Symplectic integration: a canonical map, not an exact energy promise
records.section: Reproducible notebook and checks#
records.text:
from numart.hamiltonian import trajectory, energy, canonical_step, J
t, z = trajectory(h=0.2, steps=1000, method='yoshida4', system='quartic')
print(max(abs((energy(z, 'quartic')-energy(z[0], 'quartic'))/energy(z[0], 'quartic'))))
_, M = canonical_step([0.7, 0.4], 0.2, 'yoshida4', 'quartic', True)
print(M.T @ J @ M - J)
The computed dataset and source manifest supplies 30 Python trajectories: five methods, two Hamiltonians, and h = 0.1, 0.2, or 0.4, all to T = 200 from (q,p) = (1,0.2). Plotted trajectories contain at most 1001 samples; maximum energy errors use every integration step. The phase-patch view applies one step to a square centered at (0.7,0.4). Its sampled polygon boundary is an illustration; the displayed local defect uses an analytic map Jacobian at the patch center.
Tests check refinement orders against the exact oscillator, analytic Jacobians against independent finite differences, the canonical identity on both potentials, time reversal for symmetric methods, the Verlet quadratic invariant, and the difference between quadratic and nonquadratic midpoint energy. The gallery and notebook are educational fixed-step examples, not orbit-accuracy or timing rankings.

records.title: Symplectic integration: a canonical map, not an exact energy promise
records.section: Connecting to particle gravity#
records.text:
A fixed step and a force that is the gradient of a consistent position-dependent potential support the splitting argument. A generic approximate Tree force, changing opening decisions, ad hoc mesh interpolation, or state-dependent step selection does not automatically retain that proof. Force approximation and time integration need joint tests. Continue with particle gravity and Poisson solvers and gravity boundary kernels.

It does not add a general splitting implementation to this chapter’s existing solver package. A lightweight fixed-input example now runs both on the same reaction–diffusion problem.

records.text:
Compare fluctuations, ergodicity and time correlations as well as mean temperature, from Nosé–Hoover and velocity rescaling to stochastic and momentum-conserving methods.

records.title: Thermostats: temperature control and distributions
records.section: Define the controlled temperature
records.text: With kinetic energy K and f active degrees of freedom, the kinetic temperature is T = 2 K / (f k_B). Count constraints and removed center-of-mass motion consistently, and separate thermal motion from streaming. State whether rotational degrees of freedom are included.

records.title: Thermostats: temperature control and distributions
records.section: Equal mean temperature does not imply equal distributions
records.text: For f independent momentum degrees of freedom with classical quadratic kinetic energy, canonical equilibrium gives 2 K/(k_B T₀) a chi-square distribution with f degrees of freedom. Its mean K is f k_B T₀/2 and variance is f(k_B T₀)²/2. Direct rescaling v ← √(T₀/T) v fixes K immediately after application, removing these fluctuations. CSVR instead uses a stochastic factor to generate fluctuations.

records.title: Thermostats: temperature control and distributions
records.section: Separate sampling from dynamics
records.text: An invariant distribution does not ensure adequate finite-time exploration. Even correct equilibrium sampling can coexist with friction- or collision-induced changes in velocity autocorrelations and diffusion. Assess integration error, heat-bath coupling time and random-seed dependence.

records.title: Thermostats: temperature control and distributions
records.section: CSVR and Langevin: shared canonical targets, distinct correlations
records.text: The new comparison is limited to small classical systems. CSVR and Langevin use matched OBABO splitting, degrees of freedom, temperature, potential and observation times. Distribution, fluctuations and correlations are separate diagnostics. The earlier BAOAB harmonic results remain in their original release.

records.title: Thermostats: temperature control and distributions
records.section: The stochastic CSVR update and its sign
records.text:
CSVR evolves the total kinetic energy stochastically and scales all momenta together. The implementation uses the 2007 kinetic-energy SDE and exact propagator, with the signed factor in the 2008 paper. Here h denotes a thermostat substep.
The same Gaussian R determines energy and sign. Momentum flips matter for a few degrees of freedom. Draw S directly from a chi-square law with f−1 degrees, with S=0 at f=1; this avoids the Gamma-construction typo identified by the original author.
dK=\frac{\bar K-K}{\tau}\,dt+2\sqrt{\frac{K\bar K}{f\tau}}\,dWc=e^{-h/\tau},\quad a=\frac{(1-c)\bar K}{f},\quad K^+=\left(\sqrt{cK}+\sqrt a\,R\right)^2+aS,\quad R\sim N(0,1),\quad S\sim\chi^2_{f-1}\alpha=\operatorname{sign}\!\left(\sqrt{cK}+\sqrt a\,R\right)\sqrt{K^+/K},\qquad p_i^+=\alpha p_i
Sources: Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling · Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes · Algorithms: stochastic velocity rescaling, author correction note

records.title: Thermostats: temperature control and distributions
records.section: Compare with the same splitting
records.text:
Both new methods use O(Δt/2)–B(Δt/2)–A(Δt)–B(Δt/2)–O(Δt/2) for MD step Δt: A moves coordinates, B applies forces and O is the thermostat. The CSVR formula uses bath substep h=Δt/2. They share a velocity-Verlet core and differ in the bath updates.
Set τ=(2γ)⁻¹ to match kinetic-energy relaxation for the force-free bath. This τ is not the friction time γ⁻¹. At f=1, signed CSVR has the Langevin transition law; a paired-noise check tests the implementation.
The earlier BAOAB example uses a different B–A–O–A–B splitting. Its release and independent linear reference remain unchanged; the new OBABO references and errors do not replace them.
\tau=(2\gamma)^{-1},\qquad p^+=e^{-\gamma h}p+\sqrt{m k_B T_0(1-e^{-2\gamma h})}\,R_{\rm phys}\quad(f=1)
Sources: Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes

records.title: Thermostats: temperature control and distributions
records.section: Three separate questions: distribution, fluctuation and correlation
records.text:
Both methods share the static canonical target. Check momentum, kinetic energy and instantaneous-temperature distributions, means and variances. Position references are analytic for harmonic systems and use separate quadrature for the anharmonic case. Matching the mean temperature alone does not check fluctuations.
Dynamic correlations depend on the method and coupling time. Measure position q, momentum p, kinetic energy K and total energy H without requiring agreement between methods. For harmonic Langevin, distinguish the continuous matrix exponential from the OBABO discrete stationary covariance/propagator. Other full-system correlations are measured with uncertainty and timestep dependence.
The exact ρK(t)=exp(−t/τ) reference applies only to the isolated bath. Full harmonic or anharmonic motion exchanges K and U, so that expression is not used as its correlation target.
CDF errors are maxima over predeclared checkpoints: five position/energy points and, for the conditional bath, three quantile points. They are not Kolmogorov–Smirnov suprema over the whole distribution. Full-system correlations use canonical-reference centering and normalization, so finite-step zero-lag values need not equal one exactly.

records.title: Thermostats: temperature control and distributions
records.section: Three separate questions: distribution, fluctuation and correlation
records.text: K=\sum_{i=1}^{f}\frac{p_i^2}{2m_i},\quad \bar K=\frac{f k_B T_0}{2},\quad T_{\rm inst}=\frac{2K}{f k_B}\frac{2K}{k_B T_0}\sim\chi_f^2,\quad \operatorname{Var}K=\frac{f(k_B T_0)^2}{2},\quad \operatorname{Var}T_{\rm inst}=\frac{2T_0^2}{f}C_X(t)=\langle(X(t)-\langle X\rangle)(X(0)-\langle X\rangle)\rangle,\qquad \rho_X(t)=C_X(t)/C_X(0)\mathbb E[K^+\mid K]=cK+fa,\quad\operatorname{Var}(K^+\mid K)=2fa^2+4acK,\quad \rho_K(t)=e^{-t/\tau}\ \text{(bath only)}

records.title: Thermostats: temperature control and distributions
records.section: Sampling limits and implementation boundaries
records.text:
Preservation from a canonical initial ensemble and relaxation from temperature-perturbed starts are distinct checks. Use independent replicas, fixed seeds and finite observation windows; separate sampling uncertainty from timestep and coupling effects. These small tests do not guarantee mixing from arbitrary starts. Correlation standard errors use the spread of products across independent replicas at each lag; they are not uncertainties of a single-trajectory time average or an effective-sample-size estimate. No independent dynamical reference is claimed for the anharmonic full-system correlations, which are not presented as having zero error.
A common scaling factor does not directly randomize momentum direction. A correct K distribution cannot rule out restricted sampling from invariant conditions such as zero total momentum in a symmetric system, or from invariant subspaces. The adopted degrees of freedom include no added constraints or removed center-of-mass mode.
For a positive bath step, at K=0 the direction is undefined, so this implementation rejects global rescaling explicitly. It does not inject an arbitrary direction as an undocumented algorithm. Nonfinite or nonphysical parameters are also checked.
Sources: Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling

records.title: Time integration and leapfrog
records.section: Time integration and leapfrog
records.text: Spatial reconstruction and time integration are independent choices. After spatial discretization, a PDE becomes an ODE system dU/dt = L(U). Accuracy, stability, monotonicity, dissipation, and cost then depend on both parts. The time integration notebook isolates the temporal choice using y′ = i y, y(0) = 1.

records.title: Time integration and leapfrog
records.section: Twelve methods on one oscillator#
records.text:
The exact solution exp(i t) follows the unit circle. Forward Euler and backward Euler are first order: the former grows on this undamped oscillator, while the latter damps it. The explicit RK2 family includes Heun / SSPRK(2,2), explicit midpoint, and Ralston. Kutta RK3, SSPRK(3,3), and SSPRK(4,3) are third order; classical RK4 and SSPRK(5,4) are fourth order. Implicit midpoint is second order and preserves the amplitude of this linear oscillator. Its phase still has error. Read the RK family chapter and use the family notebook for stage/order/SSP comparisons and nonlinear tests.
For y′ = lambda y, define z = lambda delta t. One-step amplification factors include
R_{\rm FE}=1+z,\quad R_{\rm BE}=\frac1{1-z},\quad
R_{\rm midpoint}=\frac{1+z/2}{1-z/2}.
The RK factors are the exponential Taylor polynomial through degree two, three, or four for the three RK2 variants, Kutta RK3 / SSPRK(3,3), or classical RK4 on this scalar linear equation. SSPRK(4,3) instead has a degree-four term z⁴/48; SSPRK(5,4) has an additional degree-five term. Shared scalar amplification does not make nonlinear RK stages identical. SSP properties depend on a forward-Euler bound for the spatial operator; they are not unconditional stability.

records.title: Time integration and leapfrog
records.section: Leapfrog needs two roots#
records.text:
The centered, two-step first-order-system recurrence is
y^{n+1}=y^{n-1}+2z y^n,\qquad
\xi_\pm=z\pm\sqrt{1+z^2}.
The root tending to +1 as z tends to zero carries the physical mode; the root tending to −1 carries a computational mode alternating between steps. Both roots and their multiplicities matter. For z = i sigma, distinct roots have unit modulus when |sigma| < 1. At |sigma| = 1 the repeated root can give linearly growing solutions; do not include that endpoint in a general boundedness claim. Above it, one root grows geometrically.
A starting value is required in addition to y(0). This implementation takes one RK4 step, optionally adding a real perturbation epsilon to y(1). At lambda = 0 that perturbation gives even samples equal to 1 and odd samples equal to 1+epsilon: a direct computational-mode demonstration. For the notebook’s oscillator it also perturbs the physical mode.
Time filters such as the Robert–Asselin family modify this behavior, with their own damping and accuracy tradeoffs; see Williams (2009). No filter is applied in this edition.

records.title: Time integration and leapfrog
records.section: Particle leapfrog is a different formulation#
records.text: A staggered kick–drift scheme for position and velocity, or velocity Verlet for a second-order mechanical system, is often also called leapfrog. Its variables live at different temporal locations and its symplectic interpretation uses that structure. The scalar recurrence above is not a demonstration of a complete SPH particle integrator or a proof of long-time energy conservation for general mechanics.

records.title: Time integration and leapfrog
records.section: Reproduce and read the notebook#
records.text:
from numart.time_integration import linear_trajectory, leapfrog_roots
t, y = linear_trajectory(rate=1j, dt=0.1, steps=200, method='leapfrog')
print(leapfrog_roots(0.1j))
The browser selects from Python-computed trajectories with fixed final time 20, twelve methods, seven step sizes, and three leapfrog starting perturbations. Axes expand for unstable samples. A matching time interval is not an equal-cost comparison: implicit solves and RK stages differ. Tests measure temporal refinement orders and check the leapfrog roots, alternating mode, and midpoint amplitude. These oscillator trajectories evaluate the scalar stability factor, which is algebraically equivalent to RK stages on this linear test equation; the separate family notebook evaluates full nonlinear stages.
Continue with the spatial stability laboratory, SPH, and ALE.

records.section: Adopted numerical method
records.text:
Thomas solves B u_next=u_current+dt theta b; reverse solves use B transpose. Save checkpoints every16steps and replay one block in the original order. Serialize and release the full trajectory before the separate checkpoint ownership window.
B=I+\Delta t\,\kappa A_h,\quad Bu_{k+1}=u_k+\Delta t\,\theta bp_N=h(u_N-d),\quad z_k=B^{-T}p_{k+1},\quad p_k=z_kJ_\kappa=0.01\kappa-\Delta t\sum_k z_k^TA_hu_{k+1},\quad J_\theta=0.02\theta+\Delta t\sum_kz_k^Tb

records.section: Bratu sensitivity near the discrete fold
records.text:
At six fixed points approaching the discrete Bratu fold, separate state error from linear-solve tolerance and compare against independent shooting gradients.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Implicit differentiation and adjoint methods
Restarted GMRES
Centered spatial difference
Armijo-damped Newton
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Analytic Jv, Poisson-Thomas right preconditioning and the preserved GMRES body solve tangents/adjoints. Save every rtol, returned candidate, true residual, termination and roundoff scale. Qualify the discrete oracle through shooting and separate high-precision Thomas-Newton. R2 uses a general near-neighbor-difference association in binary64 Jv; the original nonlinear residual,GMRES and tolerances are unchanged. R3 expands only stateNewtoncorrections ashi+lo,direct9productresidual and3productstateupdate. Physicalstates stayfloat64;derivative/adjointGMRES staysordinary.
Bratu nonlinear boundary-value problem
31/63 interior nodes; gaps .1/.01/.001 below the discrete-fold anchor. Every state starts at zero on the lower branch. Parse each lambda string once to binary float; the Decimal oracle evaluates exactly that float.

records.section: Bratu sensitivity near the discrete fold
records.text: The continuum fold is not the discrete fold. rtol1e-4/1e-8 targets are required; requested1e-12 is observational and unmet is never called converged. Independent accuracy of the returned gradient is a separate gate. Eigenvalue/roundoff scales are floating diagnostics, not certified intervals. Bratu J is symmetric; the nonsymmetric transpose is a separate operator control. The retained /solver/gmres/retention_adaptation text is historicalR1/R2;the newcontract explicitly overrides it for mixed-precisionSTATEsolves. ProjectedUNMET is separatelysaved.

records.section: Assumptions, units and boundaries
records.text: 31/63 interior nodes; gaps .1/.01/.001 below the discrete-fold anchor. Every state starts at zero on the lower branch. Parse each lambda string once to binary float; the Decimal oracle evaluates exactly that float.

records.section: Adopted numerical method
records.text:
Analytic Jv, Poisson-Thomas right preconditioning and the preserved GMRES body solve tangents/adjoints. Save every rtol, returned candidate, true residual, termination and roundoff scale. Qualify the discrete oracle through shooting and separate high-precision Thomas-Newton. R2 uses a general near-neighbor-difference association in binary64 Jv; the original nonlinear residual,GMRES and tolerances are unchanged. R3 expands only stateNewtoncorrections ashi+lo,direct9productresidual and3productstateupdate. Physicalstates stayfloat64;derivative/adjointGMRES staysordinary.
G(u,\lambda)=A_hu-\lambda e^u=0,\quad Js=e^u,\quad J^Tp=hu\mathcal J=\tfrac12h\sum_i u_i^2+0.025\lambda^2,\quad \mathcal J_\lambda=0.05\lambda+p^Te^uq^T(s_D-\hat s)-p_D^Tr=-p_D^Tr_D+r_{p,D}^T(s_D-\hat s)

records.section: Matrix-free VJP for distributed Bratu coefficients
records.text:
Represent8/16/32 spatial controls with two local hat weights per node; compare objective-wise adjoint VJPs with a separate full-sensitivity reference.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Implicit differentiation and adjoint methods
Restarted GMRES
Centered spatial difference
Armijo-damped Newton
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Bv uses local gather and B transpose scatter-add. Primary solves use Jv without an n-by-m matrix. One shared Poisson factor serves the one/three-objective runs on the same state. Dense hats and m tangent RHS are allowed only in the separate reference window. R2 uses a general near-neighbor-difference association in binary64 Jv; the original nonlinear residual,GMRES and tolerances are unchanged. R3 expands only stateNewtoncorrections ashi+lo,direct9productresidual and3productstateupdate. Physicalstates stayfloat64;derivative/adjointGMRES staysordinary.
Bratu nonlinear boundary-value problem
63 interior nodes; a(x)=2+B theta with theta=.2sin(2pi xi)+.1cos(pi xi). State/sensitivity have fixed zero Dirichlet endpoints; endpoint coefficient controls are not fixed zero.

records.text:

Dense hats and m tangent RHS are allowed only in the separate reference window. R3 expands only stateNewtoncorrections ashi+lo,direct9productresidual and3productstateupdate. Physicalstates stayfloat64;derivative/adjointGMRES staysordinary.
G=A_hu-(2+B\theta)e^u,\quad J^Tp=q,\quad \nabla_\theta\mathcal J=B^T(e^u\odot p)a_{\rm endpoints}=[a-b,a+b],\quad\theta_{\rm endpoints}=[a-b-2,a+b-2]

python run.py --input inputs.json --output output
Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

records.text:
Implement the second barycentric formula and a full-coefficient Clenshaw recurrence. Retain the closed weights and finite Chebyshev transform on rounded nodes.
p(x)=sum_j y_j*prod_(k!=j)((x-x_k)/(x_j-x_k))R(x)=(sum_j w_j*y_j/(x-x_j))/(sum_j w_j/(x-x_j))C(x)=sum_(k=0)^n a_k*T_k(x); b_k=a_k+2*x*b_(k+1)-b_(k+2)

records.section: Natural and clamped splines versus PCHIP
records.text:
Compare C2 continuity and shape preservation on three fixed data sets: a monotone plateau, a cubic and a straight line.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Spline interpolation
PCHIP monotone cubic Hermite interpolation
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Solve a cubic B-spline collocation system and evaluate it with de Boor recursion. A separate path implements PCHIP harmonic slopes, endpoint limiting and Hermite evaluation.
Cubic splines and shape-preserving interpolation
Use actual binary64 knots and values. Natural conditions set both endpoint second derivatives to zero; clamped conditions prescribe the first derivatives from the input.
Problem figure
A saved validation figure for this execution example. Its conditions and acceptance scope are documented by this page’s checks.
Natural and clamped splines versus PCHIP
This problem’s code and validation status
Exact / reference solutions
References and checks for this execution
Reference and validation scope
Compare with exact rational second-derivative systems, rational PCHIP and SciPy 1.14.1. Fifteen endpoint records contain sixteen scalar outputs from thirteen distinct inputs. Independent Fraction formulas show plateau undershoot for the actual binary64 data.

records.section: Primary sources and review scope
records.text:
Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
SciPy 1.14.1 PCHIP documentation and selected source [accessed 2026-11-25]
Review scope / review_level: official-source-selected-lines
Selected lines 202–225, 243–254, 275–298: harmonic interior derivatives, endpoint sign and 3-slope limiter, two-point case. The original Fritsch–Butland paper has not been read in full. Own formulas are independently expressed as scalar Hermite polynomials.
SciPy 1.14.1 BSpline and CubicSpline documentation [accessed 2026-11-24]
Review scope / review_level: official-documentation-selected-definitions
Natural and clamped boundary conditions and the BSpline recurrence were read during preparation. No de Boor original full-text claim. SciPy is a secondary numerical companion; the rational second-derivative system is the independent reference.

records.title: Fixed interpolation, spline and Haar controls
records.section: Haar multiresolution: boundaries, shifts and thresholds
records.text:
Apply three-level Haar analysis to short signals of lengths 17 and 32, separating one-sample shifts from odd-length boundary handling.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Wavelets
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Implement pair-sum and pair-difference filters, downsampling and inverse pyramids. Reconstruct with no threshold, hard thresholding and soft thresholding from the same analysis coefficients.
Discrete Haar transforms of finite signals
At each odd-length level append the first sample for periodic extension or the last for symmetric extension, then crop during synthesis. Apply threshold 0.2 only to detail coefficients.
Problem figure
A saved validation figure for this execution example. Its conditions and acceptance scope are documented by this page’s checks.
Haar multiresolution: boundaries, shifts and thresholds
This problem’s code and validation status
Exact / reference solutions
References and checks for this execution
Reference and validation scope
Use twelve analyses and thirty-six reconstructions. Check independent matrices, Fraction/Decimal coefficients, perfect reconstruction and squared L2 errors. Require the orthogonal error identity only at length 32; retain level-by-level padding energy at length 17.

records.section: Finite-amplitude Schnakenberg transient: nonlinearity and independent reference
records.text:
Compare raw L1/L2/L∞ with a spatially independent cosine Fourier–Galerkin/Radau reference (K32/64/96, cubic projection M=4(K+1)>4K, analytic Jacobian). Separately check K and ODE-tolerance sensitivity. Measure time order against a separately implemented Radau integration of the SAME FD semidiscretization. Norms are per-species mean-absolute/RMS/maximum, then the worse species. Record source/sink balance, every-step positive concentrations, initially absent k≥5 (first allowed k6 here), and departure from linearization. Convergence norms and reference sensitivities are assessed at the fixed final time; intermediate snapshot errors are separate evolution diagnostics.

records.title: Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation
records.section: Verification limits and failures
records.text: A selected-symmetry1D educational model: no test of free noise-driven wavenumber selection, phase stability,2D spots or biological calibration. Not an original-paper reproduction. Implicit midpoint is A-stable but not L-stable or unconditionally positive; reactions do not conserve u+v. The initial coarse protocol failed; temporal resolution was strengthened while retaining every acceptance threshold and the failed record. No quantum calculations. Near-saturation refers to the reference90→100 test window; it proves no exact steady state, nonlinear stability or long-term attractor. A huge late linearized difference diagnoses failure of linearization, not numerical error.

Methods used

Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.

This example’s formulation and conditions

records.section: Jacobian-free Newton–Krylov with analytic, central-FD and directional-AD products
records.text:
Solve both Bratu branches with three Jv choices without assembling the nonlinear Jacobian; retain forcing, actual residuals and evaluation counts.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Jacobian-free Newton-Krylov
Restarted GMRES
Thomas tridiagonal elimination
Automatic differentiation
Centered spatial difference
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Use analytic Jv, a two-residual central difference, or one-direction forward AD. Apply a Poisson Thomas right preconditioner with two-pass reorthogonalized GMRES/Givens. Start eta=.3, then clamp .9*(Fk/Fk-1)^1.5 to [.001,.5]. This is an explicit EW Choice2-style variant, not the paper’s full safeguards or PETSc defaults.
Bratu nonlinear boundary-value problem
The same dimensionless one-dimensional Dirichlet problem at lambda=3, 63/127 interior nodes, starting from zero or 4sin(pi*x). Twelve mode/grid/branch solves plus one analytic-Jv constant-eta=1e-8 control. GMRES restart24/max96, at most 24 Newton steps and nonlinear tolerance1e-9.

records.title: Double Mach reflection: lightweight grid verification
records.section: Verification limits and failures
records.text: The reference is finite-grid numerical data, not an exact2D solution or an Athena/LAVA execution. The HLL family is shared, but reference spatial operators are separately written and not imported by the primary. The reference increment is an uncertainty diagnostic, not an error bound. Initial projection, sampled moving boundaries, discretization and finite-reference effects all enter the difference; the slope is no rigorous order or full reflection-pattern convergence proof. The upper-front discrepancy stays2cells while its physical width shrinks. Fixed near-wall ROIx in[1,2.75],y<=.25 is not feature tracking. Finest ROI maxu12.644 versus reference16.125 shows the thin wall jet/roll-up is unresolved. Forward step, other wall data, general perturbations, higher order and full-pattern convergence are unverified.

Disjoint cell-local random pairs with even/odd finite-N physical-time sigma*g acceptance,energy-based safe majorant and predeclared bounded subcycling; no probability caps. \partial_t f+v_x\partial_x f=Q_{\mathrm{HS}}(f,f),\quad \sigma=\pi d^2=1/\sqrt{2}P_{ij}=n\langle c_i c_j\rangle,\quad q_x=\frac{n}{2}\langle c_x|\mathbf c|^2\rangle,\quad\mathbf c=\mathbf v-\mathbf up_{ij}=a_N W\sigma g_{ij}\Delta t/V,\quad a_N=\begin{cases}N-1&N\text{ even}\\N&N\text{ odd}\end{cases}g_{ij}\le\sqrt{2\sum_i|\mathbf v_i-\mathbf v_{cm}|^2}

records.title: Euler double rarefaction: positivity at every stage
records.section: Euler double rarefaction: positivity at every stage
records.text:
Evolve the existing strong double rarefaction on 128/256/512 cells, connecting mean-preserving positivity scaling to MUSCL, global LF fluxes and SSPRK(3,3). Log density, pressure and boundary budgets for every FE substep and SSP convex combination.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Lax–Friedrichs
MUSCL reconstruction
Mean-preserving positive-state scaling
SSPRK(3,3)
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Unlimited conservative central linear reconstruction is scaled toward its mean with one common theta per cell until both endpoint densities/pressures are positive. The two endpoint mean remains the original conserved mean. Shared LF FE updates are combined by SSPRK(3,3), reconstructing/limiting before every flux stage. Epsilon1e-13 is a reconstruction target, not an injected density/energy floor. No average repair or hidden time-step retries are used.
Compressible Euler equations
Unforced one-dimensional ideal-gas Euler at gamma=1.4 evolves cell means of density, momentum and total energy using linear conservative MUSCL reconstruction and shared Lax–Friedrichs fluxes.

records.title: Euler double rarefaction: positivity at every stage
records.section: Assumptions, units and boundaries
records.text: Fix gamma1.4, x in [0,1], discontinuity x0=.5, outer primitive states(1,-2,.4)/(1,2,.4) and T=.15. The low-density central state remains strictly positive; this is not a vacuum-generating case. Use fixed global LF splitting speed a4 and dt*a/dx<=.4; assert every actual endpoint satisfies |u|+c<=a and the sufficient dt*a/dx<=1/2 condition.

records.title: Euler double rarefaction: positivity at every stage
records.section: Adopted numerical method
records.text:
Unlimited conservative central linear reconstruction is scaled toward its mean with one common theta per cell until both endpoint densities/pressures are positive. The two endpoint mean remains the original conserved mean. Shared LF FE updates are combined by SSPRK(3,3), reconstructing/limiting before every flux stage. Epsilon1e-13 is a reconstruction target, not an injected density/energy floor. No average repair or hidden time-step retries are used.
\partial_t U+\partial_x F(U)=0,\qquad U=(\rho,m,E)^T,\quad F=(m,m^2/\rho+p,(E+p)m/\rho)^T,\quad p=(\gamma-1)(E-m^2/(2\rho))U_i^{\pm}=\bar U_i\pm\delta U_i,\qquad\widehat U_i^{\pm}=\bar U_i+\theta_i(U_i^{\pm}-\bar U_i),\quad0\le\theta_i\le1,\qquad\tfrac12(\widehat U_i^-+\widehat U_i^+)=\bar U_i\widehat F_{i+1/2}=\tfrac12\!\left[F(\widehat U_i^+)+F(\widehat U_{i+1}^-)-a(\widehat U_{i+1}^--\widehat U_i^+)\right],\qquad\mathcal E_{\Delta t}(\bar U)_i=\bar U_i-\frac{\Delta t}{\Delta x}(\widehat F_{i+1/2}-\widehat F_{i-1/2})U^{(1)}=\mathcal E_{\Delta t}(U^n),\qquad U^{(2)}=\tfrac34U^n+\tfrac14\mathcal E_{\Delta t}(U^{(1)}),\qquad U^{n+1}=\tfrac13U^n+\tfrac23\mathcal E_{\Delta t}(U^{(2)})a\ge\max_{i,\pm}(|u(\widehat U_i^\pm)|+c(\widehat U_i^\pm)),\qquad\frac{a\Delta t}{\Delta x}\le\tfrac12,\qquad\rho(\widehat U_i^\pm)>0,\quad p(\widehat U_i^\pm)>0

records.title: Euler double rarefaction: positivity at every stage
records.section: Verification limits and failures
records.text: Evidence covers this one P1 FV update and fixed input, not general MUSCL/WENO/DG, characteristic reconstruction, reflecting walls, vacuum generation or multidimensional positivity. Unlimited central slopes have no TVD, maximum-principle or nonoscillation guarantee. Raw pressure is evaluated only where raw density is positive; nonpositive raw density has its own count. Reference pressure is p(mean conserved q), not mean pressure. Gallery plots are saved one-dimensional x-t fields, not two-dimensional flow. No ExactPack or separate PDE engine is executed.

records.text:
Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
Xiangxiong Zhang and Chi-Wang Shu (2010). On positivity-preserving high order discontinuous Galerkin schemes for compressible Euler equations on rectangular meshes [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1016/j.jcp.2010.08.016
Review scope / review_level: author manuscript selected sections actually inspected: §2 Theorem2.1, Remarks2.2/2.4/2.6/2.7; §4.3 distinguishes vacuum input
Inspected positivity conditions, LF proof, stage limiting and speed-bound caution. This applies the framework to P1 FV; it does not reproduce the paper’s vacuum test or third-order DG scheme.
David I. Ketcheson, Randall J. LeVeque and Mauricio J. del Razo (2020). Riemann Problems and Jupyter Solutions: The Euler equations of gas dynamics [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1137/1.9781611976212
Review scope / review_level: official chapter sections Riemann invariants, exact solution, symmetric expansion and vacuum; official exact_solvers/euler.py integral_curve_1/3 inspected read-only
Read the official invariants, symmetric expansion and vacuum conditions. The fixed values inherit the existing atlas case and differ from this chapter’s example. No Clawpack software is executed or copied.

records.text: The reference is separately implemented but shares the HLL family and Heun; no external AMROC,LAVA or RKDG engine was executed. Without special corner treatment, a numerical entropy layer may be advected downstream; no agreement with corrected originalPPM fine structures is claimed. Whole-fluid differences,Linf and fixed corner density/pressure/entropy diagnostics are retained. Slopes do not prove pure spatial order; thin slip lines,roll-up,general geometries and high-order convergence remain unverified. Normalized maximum density differences=.592/.670/.665 do not decrease. Corner minima of log(p/rho^gamma)=-.0784/-.1224/-.3510 change substantially. This absolute entropy variable includes an arbitrary additive constant; a more-negative value is not itself an error increase. Neither stable corner extrema nor pointwise pattern convergence is established.

A graph based on row-relative off-diagonal strength supplies greedy star aggregates; leftover nodes attach to adjacent aggregates. records.section: SHAKE and RATTLE: constraints and momentum ownership
records.text:
Ten fixed pendulum evolutions distinguish position constraints, full-time tangent momentum and interior centered momentum.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
SHAKE constrained integration
RATTLE constrained integration
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Original scalar Newton position constraints, RATTLE final tangent impulses and SHAKE position pairs. SHAKE momentum is centered only at interior nodes; endpoint momenta are absent. SHAKE solves columns are eta, eta/h^2, position residual and Newton updates. Column1 uses the uniform recurrence normalization eta/h^2. For the first constrained half-step startup, the physical multiplier is 2*eta/h^2; later full position-Verlet steps use eta/h^2. Reverse-pair steps all use the later recurrence convention. RATTLE has its separate five-column normalization. No scientific gate or plot uses SHAKE column1.

Methods used

This example’s formulation and conditions
Original central-force KDK Verlet. Fixed, replayed and regenerated schedules are distinct. Positive radial crossings of cubic Hermite trajectories are localized by brentq.
Kepler two-body problem

records.title: Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification
records.section: Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification
records.text:
An inward spherical Guderley shock in cold stationary gas is evolved from t=-1 to -0.85 on 128/256/512 radial shells. HLL fluxes and Heun steps are checked against a similarity eigenvalue/field, shock trajectory and discrete conservation budgets.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
HLL
Heun / SSPRK(2,2)
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
First-order spherical finite volumes use face area4pi*r^2 and shell volume4pi*delta(r^3)/3. Shared HLL flux divergence plus the radial-momentum pressure source p_i*delta(A)/V is advanced by Heun at CFL0.4. The center is reflecting with zero face area; the outer similarity state is evaluated at both actual RK times. All three conserved budgets integrate the actual boundary flux and geometric source using the same Heun weights. There are no state floors, pressure repairs or hidden step retries.
Compressible Euler equations
The one-dimensional spherical-radial ideal-gas Euler system with zero upstream pressure and gamma=1.4. The fixed input defines a pre-collapse interval, similarity initial field, boundaries and shell averaging.

records.title: Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification
records.section: Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification
records.text: The33 unit checks and55 gates over three refinements were fixed before execution and passed with warnings treated as errors. Checks cover the zero-sound-speed cold HLL branch, geometric static-pressure balance, shared-flux budgets, actual two-stage boundary times and raw failed-stage retention. Full-volume L1 is shown alongside the predetermined r>=0.8*Rs shock/nonzero-flow region, so cold inner gas does not hide active errors. Maximum density/pressure differences and the saved shock trajectory remain visible. The semi-analytic reference uses the pinned LANL ExactPack eigenvalue routine and ODE through a cached pre-collapse-only adapter. It is not an independently reimplemented similarity ODE; the separately implemented finite-volume Euler evolution is compared against that reference. records.section: Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification
records.text: The pre-collapse branch of the spherical Guderley similarity solution at gamma=1.4 with a cold uniform upstream state. Eigenvalue shooting, similarity-ODE integration and shock-split shell quadrature make it semi-analytic rather than closed-form exact cell means. Routine replay reuses lambda from the retained qualification, freshly integrating the similarity ODE and quadrature; recomputing the eigenvalue and original ExactPack probes is a separate explicit command. This is an adapter to pinned ExactPack, not an independently implemented similarity evaluator. Collapse at the origin, the reflected shock and general equations of state remain outside this example.

records.title: Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification
records.section: Assumptions, units and boundaries
records.text: Fix gamma=1.4, three-dimensional spherical symmetry on r in [0,0.75], Rs(-1)=0.6 and t in [-1,-0.85]. Ahead of the inward shock the inner gas is exactly rho0=1,u0=p0=0. The outer region already contains the shocked similarity field; the entire initial domain is not a uniform cold state. Initial conserved shell means use order16 Gauss integration split at the exact shock, checked against order32. Reference pressure is p(mean conserved state), not mean primitive pressure.

records.title: Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification
records.section: Adopted numerical method
records.text:
First-order spherical finite volumes use face area4pi*r^2 and shell volume4pi*delta(r^3)/3. Shared HLL flux divergence plus the radial-momentum pressure source p_i*delta(A)/V is advanced by Heun at CFL0.4. The center is reflecting with zero face area; the outer similarity state is evaluated at both actual RK times. All three conserved budgets integrate the actual boundary flux and geometric source using the same Heun weights. There are no state floors, pressure repairs or hidden step retries.
\partial_t U+\frac{1}{r^2}\partial_r(r^2 F)=\left(0,\frac{2p}{r},0\right)^T,\quad U=(\rho,\rho u,E)^TR_s(t)=0.6(-t)^\alpha,\quad\alpha=1/\lambda,\quad \lambda\simeq1.3943607844,\quad t<0\frac{d\bar U_i}{dt}=-\frac{A_{i+1/2}\widehat F_{i+1/2}-A_{i-1/2}\widehat F_{i-1/2}}{V_i}+\left(0,p_i\frac{\Delta A_i}{V_i},0\right)^T\bar U_i^{\rm ref}=\frac{\int_{r_{i-1/2}}^{r_{i+1/2}}U_{\rm sim}(r,t)r^2\,dr}{(r_{i+1/2}^3-r_{i-1/2}^3)/3},\qquad p_i^{\rm ref}=p(\bar U_i^{\rm ref})

records.title: Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification
records.section: Verification limits and failures
records.text: This is a short one-dimensional spherical verification away from collapse t=0. The singular origin, reflected branch, cylindrical geometry, other gammas and nonspherical perturbation stability are untested. Two-dimensional pictures map saved spherical shell means onto a meridional plane; they are not Cartesian2D evolution. The semi-analytic field is a numerically evaluated ODE/quadrature reference, not a closed-form exact cell average. Zero pressure is allowed in the cold upstream; cancellation-band negative internal energy density down to an absolute64eps is recorded. Sound-speed square-root guards only within that band have separate counts/minimum raw pressure and do not repair the state. No general nonlinear positivity theorem is claimed. Shock-position error in cell units does not decrease monotonically:1.13/2.27/2.54. Absolute radius error is about0.00665 for the first two grids and0.00372 for the finest. Density Linf differences0.258/0.271/0.266 and pressure Linf0.492/0.494/0.466 are also not monotonically decreasing. L1 reduction is not evidence that the discontinuity is pointwise resolved or that the collapse region converges.

records.section: Assumptions, units and boundaries
records.text: All quantities are nondimensional on[0,1]², with phi<0 inside. The prescribed divergence-free rigid motion keeps the circle away from the boundary. Two exterior ghost layers receive analytic data at each RK stage; this is not a periodic boundary. Every interior value is numerically advanced. Observe0/.25/.5/.75/1; max(|u|+|v|)dt/dx<=.35.

records.text:
Both modes use the same second-order ENO one-sided differences and Heun RK2, selecting stencils by absolute second differences. Optional redistancing occurs every.1 physical time: five first-order Godunov steps, dtau=.3dx, with the smoothed sign frozen per call. There is no volume correction, interface projection, phi clipping, hidden retry or analytic interior reset.

records.title: Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation
records.section: Verification limits and failures
records.text: Sampled radial error is not a Hausdorff distance. Observed order refines dx and dt together rather than isolating spatial order. Redistancing need not improve area or position; errors increase here even on the finest grid. No numerical VOF ranking, separate PDE engine, topology change, curvature flow, surface tension or two-phase Navier–Stokes validation is claimed. The two motions are conditions of one transported-circle-interface problem.

records.section: Primary sources and review scope
records.text:
Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
S. Osher and J. A. Sethian (1988). Fronts propagating with curvature-dependent speed: Algorithms based on Hamilton-Jacobi formulations · DOI: 10.1016/0021-9991(88)90002-2
Review scope / review_level: full-text
Selected author-hosted original passages: abstract, implicit front representation and Hamilton–Jacobi transport/normal-motion formulation. No full-paper audit or reproduction of its full experiment suite.
C. W. Hirt and B. D. Nichols (1981). Volume of fluid (VOF) method for the dynamics of free boundaries · DOI: 10.1016/0021-9991(81)90145-5
Review scope / review_level: abstract-and-metadata
Publisher bibliography and abstract for the original volume-fraction formulation. No full-text algorithm audit or implementation of its donor–acceptor scheme.
M. Sussman and E. Fatemi (1999). An Efficient, Interface-Preserving Level Set Redistancing Algorithm and Its Application to Interfacial Incompressible Fluid Flow · DOI: 10.1137/S1064827596298245
Review scope / review_level: abstract-and-metadata

records.title: Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation
records.section: Primary sources and review scope
records.text:
Official abstract and bibliography: redistancing quality includes retaining the zero interface; its constrained higher-order algorithm is not the simple Godunov auxiliary iteration implemented here.
M. Sussman and E. G. Puckett (2000). A Coupled Level Set and Volume-of-Fluid Method for Computing 3D and Axisymmetric Incompressible Two-Phase Flows · DOI: 10.1006/jcph.2000.6537
Review scope / review_level: full-text
Author-hosted pp.302–305, equations(1)–(6),(9),(12),(15): signed-distance geometry, enclosed-mass issue and volume-fraction conservation. Sign is reversed here to make phi negative inside. No CLSVOF or two-phase fluid experiment executed.

records.section: 2D rigid rotation of an off-center level-set circle
records.text:
Rotate a radius.15 circle initially centered at(.68,.5) once about(.5,.5), with angular speed2pi. ENO2/Heun on32²/64²/128² grids compares optional redistancing, intermediate interfaces, geometric area and coupled grid/time refinement.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Level-set method
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Both modes use the same second-order ENO one-sided differences and Heun RK2, selecting stencils by absolute second differences. Optional redistancing occurs every.1 physical time: five first-order Godunov steps, dtau=.3dx, with the smoothed sign frozen per call. There is no volume correction, interface projection, phi clipping, hidden retry or analytic interior reset.
Level-set interface advection
Analytic circle center motion and signed distance provide references for translation and off-center rigid rotation. Interface/area errors of both modes are measured; this is not a VOF or two-phase fluid execution.

Reference and validation scope
Analytic center motion and signed distance provide the reference. Take worst errors over the four positive common observation times. Interface error samples linearly interpolated grid-edge zeros; area comes from the negative portion of a piecewise-linear triangulation between grid centers, retaining initial geometric bias. Also record phi error and distance-gradient quality in|phi_exact|<=2dx, each redistancing area jump and a separateN64 CFL-halving sensitivity.

records.title: Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation
records.section: Assumptions, units and boundaries
records.text: All quantities are nondimensional on[0,1]², with phi<0 inside. The prescribed divergence-free rigid motion keeps the circle away from the boundary. Two exterior ghost layers receive analytic data at each RK stage; this is not a periodic boundary. Every interior value is numerically advanced. Observe0/.25/.5/.75/1; max(|u|+|v|)dt/dx<=.35.

records.title: Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation
records.section: Adopted numerical method
records.text:
Both modes use the same second-order ENO one-sided differences and Heun RK2, selecting stencils by absolute second differences. Optional redistancing occurs every.1 physical time: five first-order Godunov steps, dtau=.3dx, with the smoothed sign frozen per call. There is no volume correction, interface projection, phi clipping, hidden retry or analytic interior reset.
\Gamma(t)=\{\mathbf{x}:\phi(\mathbf{x},t)=0\},\quad \phi_t+\mathbf{u}\cdot\nabla\phi=0,\quad\phi_{\rm ref}(\mathbf{x},t)=\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{c}(t)\|-0.15\psi_\tau+S_\epsilon(\phi_0)(\|\nabla\psi\|-1)=0,\quad S_\epsilon(z)=z/\sqrt{z^2+\Delta x^2}E_\Gamma=\max_{t\in\{.25,.5,.75,1\}}\max_{\mathbf{z}\in Z_h(t)}\left|\|\mathbf{z}-\mathbf{c}(t)\|-r\right|,\quad E_A=\max_t\left|A_h(t)/(\pi r^2)-1\right|

records.title: Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation
records.section: References and measured quantities
records.text: Analytic center motion and signed distance provide the reference. Take worst errors over the four positive common observation times. Interface error samples linearly interpolated grid-edge zeros; area comes from the negative portion of a piecewise-linear triangulation between grid centers, retaining initial geometric bias. Also record phi error and distance-gradient quality in|phi_exact|<=2dx, each redistancing area jump and a separateN64 CFL-halving sensitivity.

records.title: Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation
records.section: Verification limits and failures
records.text: Sampled radial error is not a Hausdorff distance. Observed order refines dx and dt together rather than isolating spatial order. Redistancing need not improve area or position; errors increase here even on the finest grid. No numerical VOF ranking, separate PDE engine, topology change, curvature flow, surface tension or two-phase Navier–Stokes validation is claimed. The two motions are conditions of one transported-circle-interface problem.

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
S. Osher and J. A. Sethian (1988). Fronts propagating with curvature-dependent speed: Algorithms based on Hamilton-Jacobi formulations · DOI: 10.1016/0021-9991(88)90002-2
Review scope / review_level: full-text
Selected author-hosted original passages: abstract, implicit front representation and Hamilton–Jacobi transport/normal-motion formulation. No full-paper audit or reproduction of its full experiment suite.
C. W. Hirt and B. D. Nichols (1981). Volume of fluid (VOF) method for the dynamics of free boundaries · DOI: 10.1016/0021-9991(81)90145-5
Review scope / review_level: abstract-and-metadata
Publisher bibliography and abstract for the original volume-fraction formulation. No full-text algorithm audit or implementation of its donor–acceptor scheme.
M. Sussman and E. Fatemi (1999). An Efficient, Interface-Preserving Level Set Redistancing Algorithm and Its Application to Interfacial Incompressible Fluid Flow · DOI: 10.1137/S1064827596298245
Review scope / review_level: abstract-and-metadata

records.title: Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation
records.section: Primary sources and review scope
records.text:
Official abstract and bibliography: redistancing quality includes retaining the zero interface; its constrained higher-order algorithm is not the simple Godunov auxiliary iteration implemented here.
M. Sussman and E. G. Puckett (2000). A Coupled Level Set and Volume-of-Fluid Method for Computing 3D and Axisymmetric Incompressible Two-Phase Flows · DOI: 10.1006/jcph.2000.6537
Review scope / review_level: full-text
Author-hosted pp.302–305, equations(1)–(6),(9),(12),(15): signed-distance geometry, enclosed-mass issue and volume-fraction conservation. Sign is reversed here to make phi negative inside. No CLSVOF or two-phase fluid experiment executed.

records.title: Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification
records.section: Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification
records.text:
Both finite-volume variants use the same unlimited centered primitive-MUSCL reconstruction, the physical Euler flux and SSPRK(3,3); only Roe dissipation is replaced by D=P^-1|PA|. At each Roe state use the total-speed Mach with mu=min(1,max(M_local,M_infinity)) and delta=1/mu-1, applying the primitive Miczek matrix through conserved-variable Jacobians. A degree-two characteristic polynomial applies the matrix absolute value; a separate dense eigendecomposition checks it. Physical time and sound speed are unchanged; acoustic CFL=0.2 remains. Reconstructed faces and all three stages check positive density and pressure, without limiters, floors, repair, hidden retries or pseudo-time iteration. A forward-Euler amplification counterexample prevents claiming SSP/TVD or general nonlinear stability from the integrator name.
Compressible Euler equations
Unforced 2D ideal-gas Euler is advanced in the original conservative variables and physical time. Fixed inputs use gamma=1.4, a periodic 20×20 box and a consistently scaled isentropic vortex with Mach-dependent background pressure.

records.text: The original 32 unit tests passed, but one of 143 first-order spatial gates failed: finest M_infinity=0.01 whole-domain dynamic pressure error 0.16537 exceeded the fixed 0.1 threshold. Original sources, contract, all twelve fields and the failed global pressure plot are retained. Revision 2 gives both fluxes the same unlimited centered primitive MUSCL and adds three checks for reconstruction, raw face failure and actual-RHS linearization against independent matrices. Inputs, physical time, CFL and acceptance bytes are unchanged; the revised 35-test/143-gate contract was frozen before revision execution. Checks cover Roe conserved jumps and physical-flux differences, dense-matrix dissipation, the three stages and raw invalid-stage retention. Each background Mach/flux has 17^2 constant-state Fourier modes and powers 1/10/100 in stated physical acoustic-energy variables. Pressure errors divide by rho_infinity*|U_infinity|^2 rather than the large p_infinity; velocity errors divide by analytic vortex perturbations. Initial R_h-q_t for the translating analytic field is retained as truncation error, not converged steady residual. Revision 2 passed all 35 tests, twelve runs and 143 gates with -W error, taking about 4.4 seconds on the original Mac. At finest M_infinity=0.01, relative velocity L1 was 0.07411 for Roe and 0.01847 for preconditioning; fixed-core pressure errors were 0.04871

records.title: Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification
records.section: Verification limits and failures
records.text: This is a short T=0.1 fixed-input, few-grid test, not a full circulation or long-time preservation study. The Fourier check covers selected uniform states, wave numbers and powers; it is no proof for all modes, nonlinear variable states or general positivity. Actual integration retains the acoustic CFL and does not use the displayed convective diagnostic step. Steady convergence acceleration, dual time, shock/contact robustness, general meshes and all Mach numbers remain unverified. Finite periodic-box seams, Gauss quadrature and primitive variables evaluated from cell means remain distinct qualifications. Pressure Mach dependence and local errors are retained. Unlimited MUSCL is selected for these smooth inputs, not a limiter, TVD method or general positivity guarantee. The original box-wide pressure waves are shown in a separate full-domain failed-trial figure rather than hidden by the gallery core crop. Velocity/core improvements do not imply globally better pressure: finest whole-domain pressure L1 is slightly larger with preconditioning and grows when background Mach is reduced by ten. No Mach-independent pressure accuracy follows from these measurements. Perturbation kinetic energy is a diagnostic computed from conserved cell means, not exact conservation of continuous kinetic energy.

This example’s formulation and conditions
Couple Yee and midpoint ADE updates to a trapezoidal derivative-memory filter at native times. Separate positive physical dissipation from signed numerical PML work, retaining all physical and auxiliary states.

records.text:
Use five long trajectories: three joint grid/layer-strength resolutions, a normal control and a weakly damped companion. Reuse the byte-bound no-PML reference only after checking every unchanged reference argument. Retain the old 13 test bodies and add two parameter-policy/peak-12 work regressions; all original 44 long-trajectory gates remain unchanged.
Same-problem reference · Finite-grid numerical reference
Isolated same-grid reference for a long grazing dispersive packet
The central angle is 80 degrees; finite kx bandwidth gives neighboring angles. The no-PML reference shares the discretization and initialization to isolate boundary error from bulk dispersion. Small operator and finite-trajectory checks do not prove global stability for arbitrary angles and materials. The joint family does not measure fixed-PML spatial order; the older 100 checks alone do not prove peak-12 global stability.

records.section: Oblique s/p incidence on a Lorentz-dispersive slab
records.text:
Reference and validation scope
Measure omega = 5.1/6/6.9 from 12 actual material/vacuum evolutions across three resolutions and both polarizations. Check an independent finite-window vacuum geometric sum, complex Fresnel coefficients, direct volume dissipation, all-step PEC budgets and final monitor tails.
Same-problem reference · Analytic reference
Complex oblique Fresnel coefficients and direct Lorentz-slab loss
This is a genuine single-ky restriction rather than arbitrary transverse data. It covers one passive Lorentz pole and a fixed finite band/window. Gaussian tails are nonzero; window diagnostics and reference errors are reported separately. No strict all-frequency no-return proof is claimed.

records.section: Adopted numerical method
records.text:
Use the single-ky Yee spatial operator and local implicit-midpoint Lorentz ADE. Couple both p-polarized electric components to polarization, and remove incident propagation with a matched vacuum pulse on the same grid. Accumulate direct Ohmic and material-damping work separately from modified energy.
\varepsilon_\infty\partial_t\mathbf E=\nabla\times\mathbf H-\sigma\mathbf E-\mathbf J,\quad\partial_t\mathbf P=\mathbf J\partial_t\mathbf J=f\mathbf E-\omega_0^2\mathbf P-\gamma\mathbf J,\quad f=\Delta\varepsilon\omega_0^2\varepsilon(\omega)=\varepsilon_\infty+\frac{f}{\omega_0^2-\omega^2-i\gamma\omega}+\frac{i\sigma}{\omega}

records.title: Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics
records.section: Multimodal MCMC: trapping, false reassurance and a global proposal
records.text:
Compare with analytic moments, seven declared CDF points and positive occupancy. Record per-chain occupancies/transitions, rank/folded split Rhat, bulk/tail/mean and mode-indicator ESS, and within-only ACF/ESS. Dispersed trapped chains can have a good pooled distribution yet fail between-chain diagnostics; same-mode chains can have reassuring Rhat yet fail the known target. A control scenario passes when its intended failure is detected. CDF error is a declared-point maximum, not whole-line KS distance or an IID-test p-value.

records.section: Assumptions, units and boundaries
records.text: Dimensionless1D target p=.5N(−6,1)+.5N(6,1), mean0/variance37/positive occupancy.5. Three fixed seeds, four chains,1024 warmup and16384 retained draws/chain. Prefixes1024/4096/16384 are nested, not independent replications. Rejections/self-transitions are retained.

records.title: Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics
records.section: Adopted numerical method
records.text:
Local scale.8; mixed uses y=−x+.8Z with probability.1, otherwise y=x+.8Z. The state-independent mixture is symmetric q(y|x)=q(x|y), so MH uses the log-target ratio. Chains use independent PCG64 streams, with no adaptation or removal of rejected states.
\pi(x)=\tfrac12\phi(x+6)+\tfrac12\phi(x-6),\quad E[X]=0,\quad\operatorname{Var}X=37F(x)=\tfrac12\Phi(x+6)+\tfrac12\Phi(x-6),\quad P(X>0)=\tfrac12q(y\mid x)=(1-p)\phi_s(y-x)+p\phi_s(y+x)=q(x\mid y),\quad s=.8,\ p=.1\alpha(x,y)=\min\{1,\pi(y)/\pi(x)\},\quad I_n=\mathbf1\{X_n>0\}

Dispersed trapped chains can have a good pooled distribution yet fail between-chain diagnostics; same-mode chains can have reassuring Rhat yet fail the known target. A control scenario passes when its intended failure is detected. CDF error is a declared-point maximum, not whole-line KS distance or an IID-test p-value.

records.title: Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics
records.section: Verification limits and failures
records.text: An educational fixed-seed, finite-budget experiment. The local Gaussian RW is theoretically irreducible MH; finite-time trapping is not called a nonergodic algorithm. Small Rhat, large ESS and pooled-CDF agreement cannot rule out undiscovered modes. Symmetry-informed reflection is not a generic multimodal solver. No quantum calculations.

records.section: Primary sources and review scope
records.text:
Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
A. Vehtari, A. Gelman, D. Simpson, B. Carpenter and P.-C. Bürkner (2021). Rank-Normalization, Folding, and Localization: An Improved R-hat for Assessing Convergence of MCMC (with Discussion) · DOI: 10.1214/20-BA1221
Review scope / review_level: corrected-author-paper-selected-sections
Checked original sections3–4, the2021-06-22 correction of Eq4.1 to denominator S+1/4, and the constant-indicator warning. This does not reproduce every original numerical experiment.
C. J. Geyer (1992). Practical Markov Chain Monte Carlo · DOI: 10.1214/ss/1177011137
Review scope / review_level: original-selected-paired-sequence-theory
Checked section3.3 and Theorems3.1/3.2 for reversibility assumptions and initial-positive/monotone sequences. Main article pp473–483 are distinguished from combined discussion pagination; no claim gives exact true ESS from finite chains.
A. Gelman and D. B. Rubin (1992). Inference from Iterative Simulation Using Multiple Sequences · DOI: 10.1214/ss/1177011136
Review scope / review_level: original-selected-multiple-chain-starting-points

records.section: Primary sources and review scope
records.text:
Checked the original introduction/section2 on multiple sequences and overdispersed starts. Distinct from the later rank/folded method, and not a reproduction of every1992 finite-sample correction.
The ArviZ developers (2024). ArviZ0.20.0 public diagnostics API and tagged source
Review scope / review_level: official-versioned-source-and-actual-independent-execution
Checked the official0.20.0 rhat/ess API and tagged source for splitting, ranks, Type7 quantiles, endpoints and constant conventions. Installed source hashes match commit94113176cae99a05ba41d1e93739ee2d5bdbe9b1;62 byte-identical datasets were actually processed in a separate environment without importing Atlas diagnostics. No upstream implementation is reproduced; values, versions, hashes and regeneration code are supplied.
N. Metropolis, A. W. Rosenbluth, M. N. Rosenbluth, A. H. Teller and E. Teller (1953). Equation of State Calculations by Fast Computing Machines · DOI: 10.1063/1.1699114
Review scope / review_level: publisher-abstract-and-metadata
Publisher bibliography and abstract checked. Cited for symmetric-proposal Metropolis acceptance; no reproduction of the original hard-sphere experiment is claimed.
W. K. Hastings (1970). Monte Carlo sampling methods using Markov chains and their applications · DOI: 10.1093/biomet/57.1.97
Review scope / review_level: original-paper-excerpt-and-metadata

records.section: Independent MCMC diagnostic checks: rank Rhat, bulk/tail ESS and degeneracies
records.text:
Actually process62 byte-identical datasets with separately installed ArviZ0.20.0, bound by recipe/input/chain/official-source hashes. Separate finite-value agreement from explicit degeneracy-policy differences.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Markov-chain Monte Carlo / MCMC
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s diagnostic and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Original equation-based implementation: split with the odd center dropped, average-tie Blom ranks using corrected S+1/4, re-rank folded deviations, and take the larger Rhat. Bulk ESS uses rank-split draws; tail ESS first determines Type7 quantiles on original full draws, then splits <= indicators. Use initial-positive/monotone pairs, declared endpoint handling and tau>=1/log10(total), without clipping antithetic ESS to N.

records.text:
References and checks for this execution
Reference and validation scope
62 datasets: nine actual chains times three prefixes times x/indicator plus eight small fixtures. Regenerate and hash identical bytes; compare ordinary finite Rhat/ESS/ACF and test constants, zero within-chain variance, odd lengths, ties, shift and scale. Direct lag sums and infinite-series stationary-AR(1) tau=(1+rho)/(1−rho) provide separate checks of finite estimates. Routine runs compare stored references; live ArviZ regeneration is a separate optional procedure.
No corresponding reference-library card is registered. The execution-specific validation material above documents its reference values and acceptance checks.

records.section: Assumptions, units and boundaries
records.text: Dimensionless1D target p=.5N(−6,1)+.5N(6,1), mean0/variance37/positive occupancy.5. Three fixed seeds, four chains,1024 warmup and16384 retained draws/chain. Prefixes1024/4096/16384 are nested, not independent replications. Rejections/self-transitions are retained.

records.title: Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics
records.section: Adopted numerical method
records.text:
Original equation-based implementation: split with the odd center dropped, average-tie Blom ranks using corrected S+1/4, re-rank folded deviations, and take the larger Rhat. Bulk ESS uses rank-split draws; tail ESS first determines Type7 quantiles on original full draws, then splits <= indicators. Use initial-positive/monotone pairs, declared endpoint handling and tau>=1/log10(total), without clipping antithetic ESS to N.
\widehat R=\sqrt{\widehat V^+/W},\quad\widehat V^+=\tfrac{N-1}{N}W+\tfrac BNz_s=\Phi^{-1}\!\left(\frac{r_s-3/8}{S+1/4}\right),\quad\widehat R_{\rm rank}=\max(\widehat R_z,\widehat R_{\rm folded})\widehat N_{\rm eff}=MN/\widehat\tau,\quad\widehat\tau=-1+2\sum_k\widehat P_k,\quad\widehat P_k=\widehat\rho_{2k}+\widehat\rho_{2k+1}\operatorname{ESS}_{\rm tail}=\min\{\operatorname{ESS}(\mathbf1[X\le q_{.05}]),\operatorname{ESS}(\mathbf1[X\le q_{.95}])\}

records.title: Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics
records.section: Verification limits and failures
records.text: An educational fixed-seed, finite-budget experiment. The local Gaussian RW is theoretically irreducible MH; finite-time trapping is not called a nonergodic algorithm. Small Rhat, large ESS and pooled-CDF agreement cannot rule out undiscovered modes. Symmetry-informed reflection is not a generic multimodal solver. No quantum calculations. ArviZ raw constant-ESS=N is not evidence of mixing. Globally identical values yield null/status; differing per-chain constants yield null/infinite-separation Rhat while retaining raw huge-finite/infinite library values outside ordinary finite comparisons. Bulk ESS is not a raw-mean MCSE estimator.

records.title: Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics
records.section: Primary sources and review scope
records.text:
Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
A. Vehtari, A. Gelman, D. Simpson, B. Carpenter and P.-C. Bürkner (2021). Rank-Normalization, Folding, and Localization: An Improved R-hat for Assessing Convergence of MCMC (with Discussion) · DOI: 10.1214/20-BA1221
Review scope / review_level: corrected-author-paper-selected-sections
Checked original sections3–4, the2021-06-22 correction of Eq4.1 to denominator S+1/4, and the constant-indicator warning. This does not reproduce every original numerical experiment.
C. J. Geyer (1992). Practical Markov Chain Monte Carlo · DOI: 10.1214/ss/1177011137
Review scope / review_level: original-selected-paired-sequence-theory
Checked section3.3 and Theorems3.1/3.2 for reversibility assumptions and initial-positive/monotone sequences. Main article pp473–483 are distinguished from combined discussion pagination; no claim gives exact true ESS from finite chains.
A. Gelman and D. B. Rubin (1992). Inference from Iterative Simulation Using Multiple Sequences · DOI: 10.1214/ss/1177011136
Review scope / review_level: original-selected-multiple-chain-starting-points

records.title: Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics
records.section: Primary sources and review scope
records.text:
Checked the original introduction/section2 on multiple sequences and overdispersed starts. Distinct from the later rank/folded method, and not a reproduction of every1992 finite-sample correction.
The ArviZ developers (2024). ArviZ0.20.0 public diagnostics API and tagged source

Run inside atlas-moving-waves-2026-11-23 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.

Reference and validation scope
Inputs/source/acceptance hashes are saved before execution. All 19 unit tests and 49 gates on three grids passed at the first attempt. Analytic density is integrated over cells by splitting shock-circle cuts and 64-point Gauss quadrature with x=rs sin(theta), checked against 128 points and analytic total mass; these are quadrature references, not closed-form exact cell means. At 128², full-square density L1=.09981, origin-inclusive core L1=.12231; shock errors are.968 axis cells and1.469 diagonal cells. Maximum relative discrete-budget residual is about 4.6e-15. D4 conserved parity and continuous rotational symmetry are measured separately.

\partial_t U+\partial_xF(U)+\partial_yG(U)=0,\quad U=(\rho,\rho u,\rho v,E)^Tr_s=t/3,\quad(\rho,p,u_r)_2=(16,16/3,0),\quad(\rho,p,u_r)_1=(1+t/r,0,-1)\bar\rho_i=\frac{1}{\Delta x\Delta y}\int_{C_i}\rho_{\rm exact}(\sqrt{x^2+y^2},t)\,dx\,dyM(t)=4R^2+8Rt\operatorname{asinh}(1)+\pi t^2,\qquad E_{\rm tot}=M/2,\quad R=0.5\Delta t=\frac{0.35}{\max a_x/\Delta x+\max a_y/\Delta y}

records.title: Noh shocks: exact reference, origin heating and refinement
records.section: Noh shocks: zero-pressure planar, cylindrical and spherical flow
records.text:
Rusanov flux with SSPRK2 (Heun). Planar/cylindrical runs retain piecewise-constant reconstruction. Spherical runs reconstruct conserved variables linearly around volume centroids with minmod slopes based on centroid distances in interior cells and zero slopes in the two boundary cells. A single theta per cell scales all conserved slopes at both faces to check face density/internal energy. Cell means are never corrected and no pressure seed/floor is used. Wave speeds, Rusanov flux and numerical stress P*=F_mom-((u_L+u_R)/2)F_mass use the same face states. The geometric CFL V/(A_La_L+A_Ra_R) uses the prescribed .35. Spherical source quadrature exactly integrates the face-linear numerical stress against 2r dr; planar/cylindrical runs keep the old arithmetic rule. Reconstructed reflection faces use even/odd parity, with physical cold inflow at the outer face. Every RK stage is checked and invalid states cause a retained failure.

records.title: Noh shocks: exact reference, origin heating and refinement
records.section: Verification limits and failures
records.text: An educational calculation: first-order space in planar/cylindrical flow and MUSCL-type limited linear reconstruction in spherical flow. Origin heating and finite-grid plateau errors remain; the center is never removed from whole-domain error. Because r^2 weighting can make central defects appear small, an origin-inclusive fixed-core norm and enlarged view are also shown. Vanishing Linf/center maximum error, high order for the complete method on smooth spherical problems, general stage positivity with the geometric source, Cartesian multidimensional flow and independent arbitrary-gamma validation are not established. Cylindrical Linf was not monotone in the old series; spherical L2/Linf and heating are retained as diagnostics. Roundoff-scale discrete mass/energy balance coexists with O(dt^2) spherical boundary-time-quadrature error against analytic totals. Radial momentum has a geometric source and is not a conserved Cartesian momentum component. ExactPack independently implements the analytic evaluator, not another numerical PDE engine.
